leftEvidence.title: The ten who spread the report die while Joshua and Caleb live

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: The men who caused complaint by bringing an evil report die by plague before the LORD.
points.right: Sirach remembers Joshua and Caleb among the spies for resisting the assembly and stopping the people from sin.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Joshua and Caleb alone remain alive from the men who investigated the land.
points.right: The other spies’ memory is cursed, while the two are preserved to receive the inheritance and show the consequences of following the LORD.

payload.posture: Numbers narrates the plague and the two survivors; Sirach turns that division into memory, warning, and inheritance.

rightEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
rightEvidence.title: Wisdom memory honors the two who resisted the congregation

payload.tension: Sirach’s moral summary is later reception rather than a replacement for the narrative’s full details.
payload.title: Ten die, two survive, two are remembered
